_readme: AECI-647 / PH-6 — docs/POSTHOG_MIGRATION_SPEC.md §AW6.
Topology + shared conventions for the PostHog observability plane. Read by apply.sh
and by scripts/ci/posthog-liveness-sweep.sh. Everything here is non-secret: the phc_
tokens are publishable and already ship in served HTML (§3.2), and the numeric project
ids are not credentials. The personal phx_ key is NEVER stored here.
IMPORTANT — see README.md §'Migration hazards' before editing a query. Two conventions
differ from Datadog and will silently zero a query if you forget them:
1. Datadog lowercased tag values on ingest. PostHog does NOT. `cache_status` is
emitted as `MISS` (apps/web/src/server-runtime.ts:989). Every query that filters a
tag whose casing is not pinned by a TypeScript union uses lower().
2. Datadog's `env:` tag is replaced by the PROJECT boundary (spec D4/§3.6), not by a
resource-attribute filter. Queries deliberately do NOT filter
`resource_attributes.env` — a wrong literal there returns 0 rows forever and looks
exactly like a healthy system.

hosts._note: us.posthog.com = management API (insights/dashboards/alerts/query). us.i.posthog.com = ingest (OTLP logs/metrics, /capture/). Swapping them yields a confusing 404 that reads like a config error (spec §2).

projects.name: aec-integrations-dev
projects._note: Dashboards land here too, deliberately: a production-only board cannot be checked against data until something reaches production, which is backwards. Alerts stay prod-only — a preview deploy failing a cron is not an incident.

alertSubscribers._note: PostHog user id, not a Supabase/D1 id. `subscribed_users` is the ONLY delivery channel apply.sh configures; Slack/Discord/webhook delivery needs cdp-functions and is deliberately out of scope (there is no Slack in this project — see CLAUDE.md).

alertDefaults._note: Hourly is the accepted floor (spec D3): `every_15_minutes` needs the Boost add-on and `real_time` needs Scale/Enterprise. Four Datadog monitors evaluated at 5–15 min; that cadence is knowingly lost (spec §3.8) and re-promotion is a one-word change here plus a plan upgrade.

tagVocabulary._note: The shared vocabulary rides as OTLP RESOURCE attributes (spec §2 invariant 4). Per-call tags (`outcome`, `trigger`, `endpoint`, `status_class`, `check`, `severity`, `table`, `index`, `route_class`, `cache_status`, …) ride as POINT attributes and are read as `attributes.<key>` in HogQL. Raw `status` was dropped in §AW1 for cardinality (§3.5) — the status code lives on the error log.

hogqlTables._note: Namespacing is asymmetric and easy to get wrong: `logs` is registered at the ROOT, while metrics and spans need the `posthog.` prefix. `FROM metrics` fails with 'Unknown table'. Verified against project 354071 on 2026-08-24.

aggregationTemporality._note: Our counters and histograms are DELTA by construction (spec §2 pins `aggregationTemporality: 1`), and gauges carry no temporality at all. So `sum(value)` is correct WITHOUT a temporality predicate, and adding one is a net risk: if PostHog ever stores the enum with different casing the predicate silently matches nothing and every counter alert reads 0 forever. If a cumulative source is ever introduced, add `AND m.aggregation_temporality = 'delta'` to the counter/histogram queries and split the cumulative ones onto argMax().

_readme: The heartbeat registry for scripts/ci/posthog-liveness-sweep.sh — the external CI
replacement for all eight Datadog `notify_no_data` monitors (spec §3.4 / §AW6).
MUST STAY IN SYNC WITH apps/api/src/lib/cron-schedules.ts. That file is the source of
truth for the twelve cron expressions and is asserted byte-equal to
apps/api/wrangler.jsonc `triggers.crons` by cron-schedules.spec.ts. The `cron` field
below is a COPY for documentation; the sweep only reads `metric` and `maxAgeMinutes`.
A cron whose schedule changes without `maxAgeMinutes` changing here will either
false-alarm or stop detecting death.
`metric` is each job's always-emitted heartbeat series — emitted on EVERY run
including clean/zero ones, which is the property that makes absence meaningful.
docs/OBSERVABILITY.md flags each of these as 'always emitted, so this doubles as the
cron-liveness heartbeat'.
Only six of the twelve had a Datadog no-data monitor. The other six
(metrics-snapshot, analytics-digest, moderation-snapshot, attestation-notify,
entitlement-expiry, and the drift job's own run) gain liveness coverage here for the
first time — a deliberate widening, recorded in README.md.

crons.datadogMonitor: AECi — Retention prune not running (no daily run)
AECi — Data quality job not running (no daily run)
AECi — Moderation queue backlog (oldest pending > 48h) [liveness half of a dual monitor]
AECi — Home stats not running (no daily compute)
AECi — Algolia sync not running (no successful cron push)
crons._note: Tightened 48h → 26h. A daily job that has not run in 26 hours is already broken; 48h let a whole missed day pass unremarked.

crons.datadogMonitor: AECi — Algolia index drift (D1 ≠ Algolia) [liveness half of a dual monitor]
AECi — Linear reconciliation sweep not running (no backlog gauge)
crons._note: Relaxed 60 → 90 min. GitHub Actions cron delivery is best-effort and routinely runs several minutes late; a 60-minute window over a 15-minute job left no margin for the SWEEP's own lateness, which Datadog (evaluating continuously) did not need.

crons.datadogMonitor: AECi — WAF poll not running (no successful hourly poll)
